paperInfo.paperName: Social Science Paper 1 (Multiple Choice) - Original Practice Bank
paperInfo.instructions: Answer all questions. Choose one best answer from A, B, C or D.

paper1Questions.questionText: What is a nuclear family?

options.text: A family consisting mainly of parents and their children

paper1Questions.questionText: What is a polygamous family?

options.text: A family in which a man has more than one wife

paper1Questions.questionText: What is a genealogy?

options.text: A record showing family relationships across generations

paper1Questions.questionText: What is a totem?

options.text: A symbol identifying a clan or family lineage

paper1Questions.questionText: What is empathy?

options.text: Trying to understand another person’s feelings

paper1Questions.questionText: State one practice associated with Indigenous Religion.
What is the Bible?
Which festival celebrates the birth of Jesus?
Which festival commemorates the resurrection of Jesus?
Where is the Kaaba located?
Name one of the Five Pillars of Islam.
During which month do Muslims fast?
How is Judaism commonly described?
Why is Great Zimbabwe important?

options.text: It is a major cultural and archaeological heritage site

paper1Questions.questionText: State one way to protect a heritage site.
Who is a chief?
State one role of a traditional leader.
Give one national symbol of Zimbabwe.
What is the general voting age in Zimbabwe?
State one responsibility of a citizen.

options.text: Obeying laws and protecting public property

paper1Questions.questionText: What is democracy?

options.text: A system involving citizen participation in choosing representatives

paper1Questions.questionText: Which institution makes national laws?
Why is a secret ballot important?

options.text: It protects the privacy of the voter’s choice

paper1Questions.questionText: What is gender equality?

options.text: Fair opportunities and treatment regardless of gender

paper1Questions.questionText: What is production?
What is consumption?
What is distribution?

options.text: Moving goods and services towards markets and users

paper1Questions.questionText: Who is an entrepreneur?

options.text: A person who starts and manages a business venture

paper1Questions.questionText: What is a budget?

options.text: A plan of expected income and expenditure

paper1Questions.questionText: What is opportunity cost?

options.text: The next best alternative given up when a choice is made

paper1Questions.questionText: What is rural-urban migration?

options.text: Movement from rural areas to towns or cities

paper1Questions.questionText: What is population density?

options.text: The number of people per unit area

paper1Questions.questionText: What is a census?

options.text: A systematic count and description of a population

paper1Questions.questionText: State one effect of deforestation.
Give one way to conserve water.

options.text: Repair leaking taps and avoid unnecessary wastage

paper1Questions.questionText: What is sustainable development?

options.text: Meeting present needs while protecting resources for the future

paper1Questions.questionText: What is self-awareness?

options.text: Understanding one’s strengths, feelings and values

paper1Questions.questionText: What is negative peer pressure?

options.text: Influence that pushes a person towards harmful behaviour

paper1Questions.questionText: How can a learner resist harmful peer pressure?

options.text: Say no and seek trusted support

paper1Questions.questionText: What is adolescence?

options.text: A period of physical, emotional and social development

paper1Questions.questionText: Give one personal hygiene practice.
What should a learner do if abuse is suspected?

options.text: Tell a trusted adult or appropriate authority

paper1Questions.questionText: Give one healthy leisure activity.
Name one reliable source of health information.
What is volunteerism?

options.text: Offering time or skills willingly to help others

paper1Questions.questionText: What is corporate social responsibility?

options.text: Responsible business action that benefits society or the environment

paper1Questions.questionText: How can ICT preserve heritage?

options.text: By digitising records, photographs and oral histories

paper1Questions.questionText: State one risk of careless online sharing.
What is religious tolerance?

options.text: Respecting people with different lawful beliefs

paper1Questions.questionText: How can tourism benefit communities?

options.text: It reduces workplace injuries and hazards

options.text: An explanation of symbols used on a map

paper1Questions.questionText: Two neighbours have different religions. What promotes peaceful coexistence?

options.text: The receipt or other proof of purchase

options.text: It can guide farming decisions and risk planning

paper1Questions.questionText: A wetland provides water and animal habitat. What should the community do?

options.text: Conserve it and use it sustainably

paper1Questions.questionText: A learner is pressured to misuse a harmful substance. What is safest?

options.text: Protect the site and manage responsible tourism

paper1Questions.questionText: A school wants to reduce litter. Which approach is most suitable?

options.text: Provide bins, educate learners and organise clean-ups

paper1Questions.questionText: A family wants to save for school expenses. What is a sensible first step?

options.text: Set a savings goal and plan regular amounts

paper1Questions.questionText: A class elects a representative. What makes the election fair?

options.text: Eligible learners have a genuine and private choice

paper1Questions.questionText: Two families disagree about a shared resource. What should they do first?

options.text: Listen to both sides and identify the issue

options.text: Avoid spreading it and check with a reliable source
